title: Skeleton-to-content loading
description: Loading placeholders that mirror the final layout (same heights, columns, and spacing) for content expected within a couple of seconds, replaced by real content without layout shift. A subtle shimmer or pulse is optional and disabled under reduced motion; long or failed loads switch to explicit progress or error states.
intent: Make loading feel predictable and avoid layout shift, while still telling the truth when loading is slow or fails.
characteristics: skeleton geometry matches the loaded layout to avoid layout shift
shown only after a short delay (about 200-300ms) to avoid flashes
switch to a progress message after a few seconds
error state replaces skeleton with retry
pulse or shimmer disabled under reduced motion
interaction: Purely presentational while loading; interactive controls that do not depend on the data stay usable; content swaps in place.
responsive: Skeleton follows the same responsive rules as the content it stands in for.
accessibility: Container has aria-busy="true" while loading; skeleton blocks are hidden from assistive technology; completion or failure announced politely; no infinite animation under reduced motion.
limitations: Misleading when the final layout is unknown; use a simple spinner with text then.
Skeletons for slow loads (more than about 10s) frustrate; show real progress instead.
